title: Two Rooks: Create a Passed Pawn
subtitle: Fix one wing, then break through on the other

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter V, §29 A Difficult Ending: Two Rooks and Pawns, Example 61

narration.say: We follow the game from the initial position. Opening phase 1.
We follow the game from the initial position. Opening phase 2.

We follow the game from the initial position. Opening phase 5.

steps.title: A plan based on the pawn structure

narration.say: Black has doubled c-pawns. White plans to restrain the queenside, activate the king, and create a passed pawn.
White begins with g4, preparing a later g5. Black advances b6.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Restrain Black’s queenside advance.

feedback.*: Advance the b-pawn to b4, controlling c5.

exercise.hint: Advance the b-pawn to b4, controlling c5.

narration.say: White activates the king. Black plays b5, seeking counterplay.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Challenge Black’s queenside formation.

steps.title: Finish the first part of the plan

narration.say: White supports the queenside and brings the king to e3.
The a-pawn advances again. Black’s queenside pawns are now restricted.
White returns the rook from b1 to f1. Black doubles on the e-file.

steps.title: Remove the pawn blocking the e-pawn

narration.say: White now changes wings. The g-pawn can challenge Black’s pawn on f6.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Begin the kingside breakthrough.

feedback.*: Advance the pawn from g4 to g5.

exercise.hint: Advance the pawn from g4 to g5.

narration.say: The rook recaptures on g5. The e-pawn is now passed.
Black shifts a rook to h6. White keeps the rook active, and Black returns to e6.
White advances h4. Black plays g6, and the rook returns to g5.

steps.title: Support the passed pawn with the king

narration.say: White makes room with the rook, then advances d4.
The other rook checks from f8. Black returns to b7.
White advances the passed e-pawn. Black tries g5, and White centralises the king.
The h-pawns exchange. White keeps both rooks active.
White exchanges one pair of rooks on h7.
The remaining rook moves to f8. Black checks the king twice.
Black tries the pawn break c5. White takes it, and Black brings the rook to a3.
White advances d5. Black resigns.

steps.title: Keep freedom while restricting the opponent

narration.say: White first fixed the queenside, then created a passed e-pawn, and finally supported the central advance with the king.
The rooks retained freedom of manoeuvre while Black’s rooks had to defend weaknesses.
The winning moves followed a general plan that could be carried out with the pieces available.
